notes:
Summary: Ceres ReserveWorks is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for real-time personalization and reranking across their ad slate. Primary driver is stable unit cost and predictable tail latency under bursty traffic. They have existing on-prem inference experiments but want a managed reserved GPU pool with VPC and strict residency. Key numbers discussed: target p95 latency <= 120ms on 512-token prompts for personalization model; sustained throughput target ~ 8k tokens/sec for peak window; acceptable cold-start window 10s with KV caching to bring to SLO.

Recent call notes: - "first-line" quote from CTO: 'We need predictable tails, not just average numbers' - they emphasize business impact of tail latency on click-through. - SE feedback: prefer 2x 8-GPU nodes (A100-equivalent) for initial POC; quantized model variants for cost studies.

POC scope (agreed): - Load test profile derived from production logs (hourly peaks, 10% heavy rerank requests). - Soak test: 48-hour sustained run at 70% of projected peak to validate thermal throttling and batch behavior. - Representative prompts set included (drive): /poc/ceres/prompts.jsonl — short personalization prompts, medium rerank batches, long session history chat. - Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, cost per 1M tokens.

Risks/assumptions: - Benchmarks must be run with same tokenization + prompt templates as prod. - Data residency clause requires regional private control plane or contractual addendum. - Procurement wants 12-month commit; legal wants SLA penalties spelled out.
